question.problem:
$\,$ $1$ is not prime and $1$ is not composite.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,¬(1\text{ is not prime}\text{ and }1\text{ is not composite}) & ≡¬((1\text{ is not prime})∧(1\text{ is not composite})) \\  & ≡¬(1\text{ is not prime})∨¬(1\text{ is not composite}) \\  & ≡(1\text{ is prime})∨(1\text{ is composite}) \\  & ≡1\text{ is prime}\text{ or }1\text{ is composite}.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: $1$ is prime and $1$ is not composite
$1$ is prime or $1$ is not composite
$1$ is not prime or $1$ is not composite
